topics.topic: Module and capability responsible for materializing operation-node inputs before HTTP request preparation
questions: Which module reads StoredValue and SpooledFile payload bytes and passes materialized inputs to `service_invoker.prepare_request`, given that `service_invoker` does not know `store`?

Which module retrieves the value and file payloads named by an operation element's StoredValue and SpooledFile references before `service_invoker.prepare_request`, especially on resume and startup recovery when no in-memory payload is available?

quotes: reach_operation_element: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST run in this order: check_binding_current for the binding; a StaleBinding writes RecordOperationFailureChange with status operation_failed and detail binding_stale; then reads every input's bytes with read_value_bytes, a value port as JsonPayload of its one StoredValue's canonical bytes and a file port as FilePayload, or FileListPayload in list order for a many port, and calls prepare_request with the current operation, the instance_name the check returned, the binding's input and output ports and those payloads; a PreSendFailure writes RecordOperationFailureChange with status operation_failed and that failure's detail_code and reason as failure_detail; then for a non-read binding asks find_send_authority with the prepared request_digest; then calls send_under_authority.
judgement.why: The later notes assign payload retrieval and materialization to effects before it calls prepare_request.

topics.topic: Ordering and equality determination for submissions matching an existing contract version
questions: When submitted contract content already identifies an existing version, which A02 validity checks run before returning it, and how is equality determined before the text says to compute its identity?
Must the kernel compute the identity and look for an existing equal version before applying the current release's ceiling checks, or must it apply those checks first as the stated step order says?

quotes:
It checks the purpose rule first (A01 rule 5: a new slot name needs a
   purpose; an existing slot refuses a different one), then the A02 rule 1
   conditions in their order, naming the first failure; a bound above its
   ceiling or omitted is refused, never clamped (A02 rule 2).

It computes
   `contract_version_id` with `capability:canonical_values.content_identity`; an equal version is returned unchanged and does not
   become current again (A01 rule 4) — the A02 rule 1 ceiling checks bind only
   a new version, so an equal one is returned even after a release lowered a
   ceiling below its bounds (A20 rule 4).
judgement.why: The first passage requires the current ceiling checks before identity computation, while the second requires an existing equal version to bypass those checks.

topics.topic: Scope of A08 rule 5 installed-instance validation at startup
questions: Which A08 rule 5 checks can and must run at startup when this step has no operation name, binding proposal ports or proposed request shape?
Which record-level A08 rule 5 checks are performed at startup, and over which capability entries, when `check_installed_instances` has no proposed operation name or proposed ports to validate?

judgement.why: This is the same startup A08 rule 5 validation-scope question already decided by P1, and the relevant passages have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Startup A08 rule 5 validation scope and ordering for installed instances without operation context
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: State 8 limits startup validation to ordered service-record checks and header collisions, so no operation-specific capability checks are performed.

topics.topic: A09 pre-send failure for a configured instance absent from the service manifest
questions: At send time, which A09 pre-send failure applies when configuration selects an instance name that the service manifest does not contain?

topics.topic: Behavior when removal of a run spool fails
questions: When `store.remove_run_spool` cannot remove all files after a run ends or is released, does the triggering request succeed with deferred cleanup, or return `internal_error` and stop the kernel?

topics.topic: Module and capability responsible for materializing trial and admission inputs for sandbox execution
questions: Which module reads the bytes named by each trial case's StoredValue and file-fixture references, through which capability, and passes the decoded values and file bytes to the sandbox for try and admission executions?

topics.topic: Persistence and representation of disclosure classes for trial file outputs
questions: Does a trial file output persist a disclosure class, and if so, in which record or reference is that class represented?

topics.topic: Whether kernel startup is exempt from State 4 request-entry validation
questions: Is `flow:start_and_recover_kernel` exempt from the request size, token, operation-schema and actor checks in the State 4 preamble?
